Deploy App is built across many separate pvarki repositories — the legacy stack (docker-rasenmaeher-integration) pulls most of them in as git submodules, while the Kubernetes stack (opendefence-platform) and the per-product integration APIs live as standalone repos. This page covers the day-to-day branching, PR, and review flow that applies to all of them. For the conventions those flows enforce (Markdown style, line-endings, shared CI), see Community & Standards.

Where the code lives

There is no single monorepo. Almost every component is its own repository, and the legacy stack stitches them together as submodules. From docker-rasenmaeher-integration/README.rst:

The submodules are repos in their own right, if you plan to make changes into them change to the directory and create new branch, commit and push changes as usual under that directory.

The practical consequence: decide which repo actually owns the change before you start. A fix to the core API belongs in pvarki/python-rasenmaeher-api, not in the integration repo that happens to vendor it as the api/ submodule. See Reporting issues & support for a triage map of which repo owns what.

Standard PR flow (any repo)

  1. Fork or branch from main. Use a short, descriptive branch name (e.g. feat/matrix-room-state, fix/241-srt-passwords).

  2. Make focused commits. Keep one concern per PR — the opendefence-platform agent guidance is explicit about this for k8s/ work ("Keep changes limited to one concern per PR").

  3. Run the local checks before pushing (see Community & Standards for the shared pre-commit setup):

    pre-commit install --install-hooks
pre-commit run --all-files

    If pre-commit complains about missing environment variables in the legacy stack, run source example_env.sh first.

  4. Open a PR against main. CI runs automatically (lint/type-check, tests, container build, dependency scan — see Community & Standards).

  5. Address review, get an approval, merge.

Working with submodules (legacy stack)

The legacy docker-rasenmaeher-integration repo references its components at pinned commits. Clone and update with submodules so you get a consistent set:

git clone --recurse-submodules -j8 git@github.com:pvarki/docker-rasenmaeher-integration.git
# after pulling or switching branches:
git submodule update --init --recursive
To change a component, treat its submodule directory as a normal repo:

cd api          # e.g. python-rasenmaeher-api
git checkout -b fix/my-change
# ...edit, commit, push in THIS repo...

Then, in the integration repo, commit the updated submodule pointer so the stack picks up your change. Land the component PR first, then bump the pointer. The submodule directories and their upstream repos are listed in the integration README under "Directories that are submodules" (for example api → python-rasenmaeher-api, takintegration → python-tak-rmapi, mtxauthz → python-mediamtx-rmmtxauthz).

Working in the Kubernetes stack

opendefence-platform is a single repo (no submodules) organized as Kustomize base/ + overlays/<env>/ folders. Its agents.md is the working contract for changes under k8s/:

  • Work inside one k8s/<service>/ folder per concern; add new workloads as a base/ + overlays/<env>/ pair.

  • Keep base/ environment-agnostic; put hostnames, certificates, image overrides, and ingress in overlays/<env>/.

  • When build/deploy phasing changes, update the root taskfile.yaml in the same change.

  • Build affected overlays locally before pushing:

    kubectl kustomize --enable-helm k8s/<service>/overlays/local

    Use --enable-helm whenever the kustomization includes helmCharts (e.g. traefik, trust-manager, external-secrets-operator).

Working on a product integration

Integration APIs (e.g. python-matrix-rmapi, python-tak-rmapi, python-mediamtx-rmmtxauthz) are standalone repos scaffolded from pvarki/python-integration-template. They follow the same PR flow, plus a version bump on every change (see Releases & versioning). The matrix example's PR pipeline shows the expected gates: version-check, pre-commit, pytest, dependency scan, and a Docker build of both the test and production targets. See Build an Integration (separate book) for the development workflow itself.

Cross-stack changes

Because the legacy and Kubernetes stacks are genuinely different deployments, a behavior change in a shared component (e.g. the core rmapi) may need follow-up in both: a submodule pointer bump in docker-rasenmaeher-integration and a manifest/image update in opendefence-platform. Note which stacks you have tested in the PR description.

Commit and review etiquette

  • Conventional-style prefixes (feat:, fix:, chore:) are used across the repos and feed the release notes — keep using them.
  • Reference the issue or PR number where relevant; the legacy release notes link PRs and commits per component.
  • Keep PRs reviewable: small diffs, clear description, note any new mandatory env vars or breaking changes so they can be captured in the release notes.
